title: Adversary Complaint for Fraudulent Conveyance and Objection to Discharge
text:
IN THE UNITED STATES BANKRUPTCY COURT FOR THE SOUTHERN DISTRICT OF TEXAS
HOUSTON DIVISION

In re:    
LUMEN HOLDINGS, INC.,          Case No. 24-33189-CAG
    Debtor.                     Chapter 11

SUSAN M. WELLINGTON, solely in her capacity as
Litigation Trustee of the Lumen Holdings Litigation Trust,
              Plaintiff,
v.
NATHANIEL R. CROSS and
CROSS FAMILY INVESTMENTS, LLC,
              Defendants.

ADVERSARY COMPLAINT
( Fraudulent Conveyance – 11 U.S.C. § 548 ; Objection to Discharge – 11 U.S.C. § 727 )

Cause No. 24-04097

Plaintiff Susan M. Wellington, by and through her undersigned counsel, files this Complaint against the above-named Defendants, and in support thereof states as follows:

I.  PARTIES AND JURISDICTION
1.   Plaintiff Susan M. Wellington ("Plaintiff" or "Trustee") is the duly appointed Litigation Trustee of the Lumen Holdings Litigation Trust, with a mailing address of 2000 McKinney Avenue, Suite 1500, Houston, Texas 77010.  Plaintiff is a resident of Harris County, Texas.
2.   Defendant Nathaniel R. Cross ("Cross") is an individual residing at 412 Elm Street, Houston, Texas 77007.  Cross is the former Chief Executive Officer of Lumen Holdings, Inc.  Cross is also known as Nate Cross.
3.   Defendant Cross Family Investments, LLC ("CFI") is a Texas limited liability company with its principal place of business at 412 Elm Street, Houston, Texas 77007.  CFI is wholly owned and controlled by Nathaniel R. Cross.
4.   This Court has jurisdiction over this adversary proceeding pursuant to 28 U.S.C. § 1334 and 28 U.S.C. § 157(b)(2)(H) and (J).  This is a core proceeding.

II.  FACTUAL BACKGROUND
5.   On or about March 1, 2023, Lumen Holdings, Inc. ("Debtor") filed a voluntary petition for relief under Chapter 11 of the Bankruptcy Code.  The Debtor’s principal place of business was located at 2000 McKinney Avenue, Suite 1500, Houston, Texas 77010.
6.   Prior to the petition date, on January 15, 2023, Cross caused the Debtor to transfer an undivided interest in certain real property located at 1010 Commerce Street, Houston, Texas 77002 (the "Property") to CFI for no consideration.  The Property had a fair market value of $1,250,000 at the time of transfer.
7.   The transfer was made with the actual intent to hinder, delay, or defraud creditors of the Debtor.  Cross, knowing the Debtor was insolven

t, orchestrated the transfer to shield assets from the reach of creditors.  In a deposition, Cross admitted he "wanted to protect the family’s nest egg."

III.  LEGAL CLAIMS
8.   Count I – Fraudulent Conveyance Under 11 U.S.C. § 548(a)(1)(A).  The transfer of the Property was made within two years of the petition date, and Cross received less than reasonably equivalent value in exchange.  The transfer was made with actual intent to hinder, delay, or defraud.
9.   Count II – Objection to Discharge Under 11 U.S.C. § 727(a)(2)(A).  Cross, with intent to hinder, delay, or defraud a creditor, transferred property of the Debtor within one year before the filing of the petition.
10.  Count III – Avoidance of Transfer Under Texas Business & Commerce Code § 24.005(a)(1).  The transfer is avoidable as a constructively fraudulent transfer.

IV.  RELIEF REQUESTED
WHEREFORE, Plaintiff prays that the Court enter judgment against Defendants, avoid the transfer, and deny Cross’s discharge.  Plaintiff also requests costs and such other relief as is just.

Dated:  November 10, 2024.

                                Respectfully submitted,

                                /s/ Patricia L. Hanford

title: Adversary Complaint Seeking Substantive Consolidation and Recovery of Transfers
text:
IN THE UNITED STATES BANKRUPTCY COURT FOR THE NORTHERN DISTRICT OF TEXAS
FORT WORTH DIVISION

In re:
PIONEER PETROLEUM CORPORATION,      Case No. 24-45211-BJH
         Debtor.                     Chapter 11

JAMES T. KELLY, III, as Liquidating Trustee,
               Plaintiff,
v.
NORTH TEXAS ENERGY PARTNERS, LP;
JENNIFER L. STERLING; and
WILLIAM H. STERLING,
               Defendants.

ADVERSARY COMPLAINT
(Substantive Consolidation, Avoidance of Preferential Transfers, and Turnover of Property)

Cause No. 24-05042

COMES NOW Plaintiff James T. Kelly, III ("Plaintiff" or "Trustee"), by and through his undersigned counsel, and files this Complaint against Defendants, alleging as follows:

I.  PARTIES
1.   Plaintiff James T. Kelly, III is the duly appointed Liquidating Trustee of the Pioneer Petroleum Corporation Liquidating Trust, with offices at 500 Throckmorton Street, Suite 800, Fort Worth, Texas 76102.
2.   Defendant North Texas Energy Partners, LP ("NTEP") is a Texas limited partnership with its principal place of business at 200 Commerce Street, Fort Worth, Texas 76102.  NTEP is controlled by Defendants Jennifer L. Sterling and William H. Sterling.
3.   Defendant Jennifer L. Sterling (formerly Jennifer L. Avery) is an individual residing at 3400 Bellaire Drive South, Fort Worth, Texas 76109.  Jennifer is the wife of William H. Sterling.  She is a former officer of Pioneer Petroleum.  Her maiden name is Avery.
4.   Defendant William H. Sterling is an individual residing at 3400 Bellaire Drive South, Fort Worth, Texas 76109.  William was the Chief Financial Officer of Pioneer Petroleum until its bankruptcy filing.

II.  JURISDICTION AND VENUE
5.   This Court has jurisdiction under 28 U.S.C. § 1334, 28 U.S.C. § 157(b)(2)(A), (E), and (O).  Venue is proper under 28 U.S.C. § 1409(a).

III.  FACTUAL ALLEGATIONS
6.   On or about June 5, 2024, Pioneer Petroleum Corporation ("Debtor") filed for Chapter 11 relief.  Prior to filing, the Sterlings operated the Debtor and NTEP as a single economic entity, commingling funds and assets.
7.   On January 20, 2024, the Debtor transferred $500,000 to NTEP without receiving reasonably equivalent value.  The transfer was made for the benefit of the Sterlings, who used the funds for personal expenses, including a vacation to Cabo San Lucas.
8.   On February 14, 2024, the Debtor made a payment of $75,000 to William H. Sterling, which constituted a preferential transfer under 11 U.S.C. § 547(b).  William was an insider of the Debtor.
9.   A.B. is the minor child of Jennifer and William Sterling, and holds a beneficial interest in certain trusts that are being used to conceal assets.  A.B. is identified by initials only.

IV.  CLAIMS FOR RELIEF
10.  Count I – Substantive Consolidation.  The affairs of the Debtor and NTEP are so intertwined that consolidation is necessary to avoid injustice.
11.  Count II – Avoidance of Preferential Transfer (11 U.S.C. § 547(b)).  The $75,000 payment to William H. Sterling is avoidable.
12.  Count III – Avoidance of Fraudulent Transfer (11 U.S.C. § 548(a)(1)(B)).  The $500,000 transfer to NTEP is avoidable as a constructively fraudulent transfer.

V.  PRAYER
WHEREFORE, Plaintiff requests entry of an order consolidating the Debtor and NTEP, avoiding the transfers, and requiring turnover of assets.  Plaintiff also requests costs and attorney’s fees.

Dated:  December 1, 2024.

                                Respectfully submitted,

                                /s/ Angela M. Reeves
                                Angela M. Reeves (State Bar No. 24123456)
                                REEVES & GARCIA, LLP
                                201 Main Street, Suite 100
                                Fort Worth, Texas 76102

                                ATTORNEY FOR PLAINTIFF

title: Adversary Complaint for Determination of Nondischargeability of Debt
text:
IN THE UNITED STATES BANKRUPTCY COURT FOR THE SOUTHERN DISTRICT OF TEXAS
HOUSTON DIVISION

In re:
ROBERTA L. GONZALEZ,              Case No. 24-38921-CAG
         Debtor.                    Chapter 7

FIDELITY NATIONAL BANK,
               Plaintiff,
v.
ROBERTA L. GONZALEZ,
               Defendant.

ADVERSARY COMPLAINT
(Objection to Discharge – 11 U.S.C. § 523(a)(2)(A) and § 523(a)(4))

Cause No. 24-04112

Plaintiff Fidelity National Bank ("Plaintiff" or "Bank"), by and through its undersigned counsel, complains of Defendant Roberta L. Gonzalez ("Debtor" or "Gonzalez"), and in support states:

I.  PARTIES
1.   Plaintiff Fidelity National Bank is a national banking association with its main office at 100 Congress Avenue, Austin, Texas 78701.  The Bank is a creditor of the Debtor.
2.   Defendant Roberta L. Gonzalez (formerly known as Roberta L. Martinez) is an individual who filed for Chapter 7 relief on or about August 15, 2024.  Gonzalez resides at 1420 San Jacinto Street, Apt. 4B, Houston, Texas 77002.  Gonzalez is also known as Bobbi Gonzalez.  Her maiden name is Martinez.
3.   Gonzalez was born on March 14, 1971.

II.  JURISDICTION AND VENUE
4.   This Court has jurisdiction under 28 U.S.C. § 1334 and 28 U.S.C. § 157(b)(2)(I).  Venue is proper under 28 U.S.C. § 1409(a).

III.  FACTUAL ALLEGATIONS
5.   On November 1, 2022, Gonzalez applied for and received a credit card from the Bank, with a credit limit of $25,000.  In the application, Gonzalez made material misrepresentations regarding her income and assets, stating she earned $180,000 per year, when in fact she earned $45,000.
6.   Between November 2022 and June 2024, Gonzalez used the credit card to obtain cash advances and make purchases totaling $28,500.  She had no intention of repaying the debt.
7.   Gonzalez also acted as a fiduciary for a minor relative, A.B., and misappropriated funds from a trust account.  A.B. is the minor child of Gonzalez’s cousin.
8.   The Bank obtained a state court judgment against Gonzalez on August 1, 2024, in the amount of $31,200.  The judgment remains unpaid.

IV.  LEGAL CLAIMS
9.   Count I – Nondischargeability Under 11 U.S.C. § 523(a)(2)(A).  The debt was obtained by false pretenses, false representation, or actual fraud.
10.  Count II – Nondischargeability Under 11 U.S.C. § 523(a)(4).  Gonzalez committed defalcation while acting as a fiduciary.

V.  RELIEF
WHEREFORE, Plaintiff requests that the Court determine the debt to be nondischargeable, and award costs, attorney’s fees, and such other relief as is proper.

Dated:  January 5, 2025.

                                Respectfully submitted,

title: Adversary Complaint for Turnover and Recovery of Post-Petition Transfers
text:
IN THE UNITED STATES BANKRUPTCY COURT FOR THE SOUTHERN DISTRICT OF TEXAS
HOUSTON DIVISION

In re:
GULF COAST RESTAURANTS, INC.,      Case No. 24-40123-TMH
         Debtor.                     Chapter 11

MARTHA E. VASQUEZ, as Plan Administrator,
              Plaintiff,
v.
ALAMO FOOD SERVICES, LLC; and
HECTOR R. DELGADO,
              Defendants.

ADVERSARY COMPLAINT
(Turnover of Property – 11 U.S.C. § 542 ; Avoidance of Post-Petition Transfers – 11 U.S.C. § 549 )

Cause No. 24-04231

Plaintiff Martha E. Vasquez ("Plaintiff" or "Administrator"), by and through her counsel, files this Complaint against Defendants, and alleges:

I.  THE PARTIES
1.   Plaintiff Martha E. Vasquez is the Plan Administrator under the confirmed Chapter 11 plan of Gulf Coast Restaurants, Inc. ("Debtor"), with offices at 1100 Louisiana Street, Suite 400, Houston, Texas 77002.  Vasquez was appointed on September 1, 2024.
2.   Defendant Alamo Food Services, LLC ("Alamo") is a Texas limited liability company with its principal place of business at 800 Broadway, San Antonio, Texas 78205.
3.   Defendant Hector R. Delgado ("Delgado") is an individual residing at 4500 San Pedro Avenue, San Antonio, Texas 78212.  Delgado is the sole member and manager of Alamo.
4.   Delgado is also known as Hector R. Delgado-Morales, and was formerly known as Hector Ramirez.

II.  JURISDICTION
5.   This Court has jurisdiction under 28 U.S.C. § 1334 and 28 U.S.C. § 157(b)(2)(E) and (F).  Venue is proper under 28 U.S.C. § 1409(a).

III.  FACTS
6.   On July 1, 2024, the Debtor filed for Chapter 11 relief.  On July 15, 2024, post-petition, the Debtor (acting without court approval) transferred $150,000 in cash and certain restaurant equipment to Alamo.
7.   The transfer was made at the direction of Delgado, who was a director of the Debtor.  Delgado told the Debtor’s CEO, "I need the equipment for my new place."
8.   Alamo has refused to return the property or the cash.  The equipment includes six commercial ovens valued at $60,000.
9.   Plaintiff has identified a minor beneficiary, A.B., who holds a beneficial interest in a trust that holds assets of the Debtor.  A.B. is the child of a former officer.

IV.  LEGAL CLAIMS
10.  Count I – Turnover Under 11 U.S.C. § 542(a).  Defendants are in possession of property of the estate and must deliver it to the Administrator.
11.  Count II – Avoidance of Post-Petition Transfer Under 11 U.S.C. § 549(a).  The transfer was unauthorized and is avoidable.
12.  Count III – Recovery of Avoided Transfer Under 11 U.S.C. § 550(a).

V.  PRAYER
WHEREFORE, Plaintiff requests that the Court order turnover, avoid the transfer, and award costs, including attorney’s fees, and such other relief as is just.

Dated:  February 1, 2025.

                                Respectfully submitted,

                                /s/ Karen L. Whitfield
                                Karen L. Whitfield (State Bar No. 24145678)
                                WHITFIELD & ASSOCIATES, PLLC
                                1300 Smith Street, Suite 500
                                Houston, Texas 77002

                                Email: kwhitfield@whitfield-law.com
                                ATTORNEY FOR PLAINTIFF

CERTIFICATE OF SERVICE
I certify that a true copy of the foregoing was served on all defendants and their counsel via CM/ECF on February 1, 2025.

title: Adversary Complaint for Injunction and Recovery of Estate Assets
text:
IN THE UNITED STATES BANKRUPTCY COURT FOR THE SOUTHERN DISTRICT OF TEXAS
HOUSTON DIVISION

In re:
TRIDENT CONSTRUCTION CO.,          Case No. 24-41098-CAG
         Debtor.                     Chapter 7

EDWARD P. HARRISON, Chapter 7 Trustee,
               Plaintiff,
v.
BEACON SUPPLY CHAIN, INC.; and
CLAIRE M. DUVALL,
               Defendants.

ADVERSARY COMPLAINT
(Preliminary Injunction, Turnover, and Avoidance of Unauthorized Transfers)

Cause No. 24-04351

Plaintiff Edward P. Harrison ("Plaintiff" or "Trustee"), by and through his counsel, states:

I.  PARTIES
1.   Plaintiff Edward P. Harrison is the Chapter 7 Trustee of the estate of Trident Construction Co. ("Debtor"), with a mailing address at 1400 Post Oak Boulevard, Suite 300, Houston, Texas 77056.
2.   Defendant Beacon Supply Chain, Inc. ("Beacon") is a Texas corporation with its principal place of business at 5000 Westheimer Road, Houston, Texas 77056.
3.   Defendant Claire M. Duvall ("Duvall") is an individual residing at 2100 Kirby Drive, Apt. 8, Houston, Texas 77019.  Duvall is the sole shareholder and president of Beacon.  Duvall is also known as Claire M. Duvall-Simpson, and was formerly known as Claire M. Simpson.  Her maiden name is Simpson.
4.   Duvall was born on March 14, 1971.

II.  JURISDICTION
5.   This Court has jurisdiction over this adversary proceeding under 28 U.S.C. § 1334 and 28 U.S.C. § 157(b)(2)(A), (E), and (N).  Venue is proper under 28 U.S.C. § 1409(a).

III.  FACTUAL BACKGROUND
6.   On October 1, 2024, the Debtor filed for Chapter 7 relief.  On October 5, 2024, Duvall, who was the Debtor’s former vice president, caused the Debtor to transfer $200,000 in cash and several construction vehicles to Beacon.
7.   The transfers were made after the petition date and without court authorization.  Duvall used the funds to purchase a personal residence at 1200 Kirby Drive.
8.   Beacon currently holds $150,000 in a bank account at Texas Commerce Bank, account number ending in 7890.
9.   The Trustee has discovered that a minor, A.B., is the beneficiary of a trust that holds an interest in certain assets transferred to Beacon.  A.B. is the child of Duvall’s sister.

IV.  CLAIMS
10.  Count I – Preliminary Injunction.  Defendants are dissipating estate assets, and immediate injunctive relief is necessary.
11.  Count II – Turnover Under 11 U.S.C. § 542.  Defendants are in possession of estate property.
12.  Count III – Avoidance Under 11 U.S.C. § 549 and Recovery Under § 550.  The post-petition transfers are avoidable.

V.  RELIEF REQUESTED
WHEREFORE, Plaintiff prays that the Court issue a preliminary injunction, order turnover, avoid the transfers, and award costs, including attorney’s fees, and such other relief as is just.

Dated:  March 1, 2025.

                                Respectfully submitted,
